formal.anchor: KnowledgeOS should not initially be modelled as merely an infinite-dimensional vector space. A more general and safer starting point is: K=(X,tau) where X is the space of possible knowledge states/knowledge elements and tau is a topology describing which knowledge states or elements are considered structurally close/connected. The vector-space structure can then be introduced if and where it is justified.

governance.anchor: I would not yet declare the infinite-dimensional vector-space model canonical. Instead: Set -> Topology -> Dimension -> Metric/Geometry -> Vector/Function Space -> Probability. We first establish the weakest structure necessary. Then add stronger structures only when required. What is the minimum mathematical structure required to represent KnowledgeOS knowledge states, evolving dimensions, values, epistemic boundaries, relationships and transformations? My current hypothesis is: KnowledgeOS requires at least a structured state space with an evolving topology and dimension system. Whether that structure is ultimately a topological vector space, manifold, simplicial complex, sheaf, graph-induced topology, measurable space, probability space, or a hybrid is still open.

rationale_evidence.statement: Identifies S2293's topological lens as the first non-Gita lens introduced in the track, but finds it is a RE-ENTRY, not a genuinely new lens: two prior uncited corpus files already cover topological material, one of them (boundaries, connectedness, failure modes) directly relevant to artifact 28's four failure modes. Registers L-Q1: check existing material before extending it (an instance of the project's own canonical-discovery rule, R-Q2). Also notes the topological lens hits the same missing-structure gap as every dynamic statistical match in artifact 17: it needs a notion of nearness (open sets, neighbourhoods, or a metric), and Sigma's five axes remain 0-of-5 ordered.
